findings.subject: PLAN-050.05
findings.title: ARCH-012's central claim that no concern is ready for extraction is already contradicted by tracked code: the idea-realization plugin, treated throughout the study's evidence as merely 'planned' and having 'no implemented writer,' is now a fully built, tested, installable plugin validated end-to-end outside this repository.
findings.evidence: `git show origin/dev:docs/08-governance/systems.yaml` shows all eight `sys-plugin*` entries still `status: planned`. `git show origin/dev:docs/09-backlog/backlog.yaml` shows `phase-plug-01` through `phase-plug-09` all `status: complete`, including `phase-plug-08: End-to-end exercise in a scratch repository, install documentation, and handover`. `git ls-tree -r --name-only origin/dev -- plugins/` returns 102 tracked files (agents, schemas, `pytest.ini`, `scripts/backlog.py`, `scripts/check.py`, etc.). `git show origin/dev:plugins/idea-realization/README.md` opens: 'A Claude Code plugin that carries an idea from capture through triage, partition, planning, phases and backlog to governed documents, in any git repository,' with install/prerequisites/scaffold/doctor steps. The study's own evidence file (`docs/00-working/boundary-study/system-backlog-review.md:16`) records that at its own baseline, 3 of the 4 occupied active-claim slots were `sys-plugin-backlog`, `sys-plugin-generators`, and `sys-plugin-ideas` — i.e. the plugin was being actively built throughout the study window. Yet ARCH-012 (lines 31-32) states: 'The evidence does not show an independently operated concern with a stable enough runtime contract, release cadence, or audience to justify immediate separation,' and the system-interface-inventory (`docs/00-working/boundary-study/system-interface-inventory.md`) describes every `sys-plugin*` row as 'planned,' 'No implemented writer,' 'planned plugin sub-area.' Phase-bnd-04's reconciliation only ran `git diff 2fd11e9..0c47c27 -- docs/08-governance/systems.yaml` (empty) to conclude the registry evidence 'remains current' — it never checked backlog/code state, only the registry file's text.
findings.consequence: The owner would be asked to choose a boundary direction from a report whose supporting evidence about 'no candidate ready for extraction' is already overtaken: a concern the report calls incubating already has a documented schema/data contract, independent tests, install documentation, and an out-of-repository validation run — several of Option B's own stated preconditions. Approving ARCH-012 as decision-ready without addressing this risks anchoring the owner's decision on stale evidence.
findings.minimal_fix: Before G3, add a one-paragraph addendum to ARCH-012 checking the plugin's actual implementation/test/install state against its registry status and Option B's precondition list, rather than relying on a registry-text diff alone as proof the evidence 'remains current.'

findings.subject: PLAN-050.03
findings.title: The corpus-wide entry-point classification (`phase-bnd-05`) is applied inconsistently across structurally identical prompts, undermining the 13/14/12/1 split ARCH-012 cites.
findings.evidence: Re-applying the rubric's entry-point question to 13 non-pilot prompts found four discrepancies: (1) PROMPT-001 is a standalone `depends_on: []` prompt 'feed to a Claude instance... to drive code generation,' never named as a step by any other governed document (`grep -rl "PROMPT-001" docs/02-prompts` returns only itself; ADR-012:95 calls it 'a reusable code-generation prompt for this system') yet is classified `sequence-factory-step`, the bucket meant for pack children like PROMPT-011 ('Child of the agent factory prompt... read at its Step 1'). (2) PROMPT-009 ('Fourth of four... Reusable, and deliberately read-only. Run it periodically... to find where the plan record and the repository have drifted apart') is classified `planning-sequence-start`, while its structural twin PROMPT-008 ('Third of four... reusable... run it repeatedly') is classified `direct-operational-entry` — both described identically as recurring, standalone, reusable work. (3) PROMPT-025 ('Prompt A'... 'pasteable seed for the planning session'... 'produces Prompt B... and nothing else') is classified `owner-launched-campaign`, while its two structural twins under the same pack-protocol shape, PROMPT-020 (pilot) and PROMPT-027 ('produces... Prompt B... and nothing else'), are both classified `planning-sequence-start`. (4) PROMPT-041, the study's own phase-runner ('Use this prompt to continue the System Boundary Study one phase at a time... not permission to execute the whole study in one session'), is classified `direct-operational-entry` alongside general-purpose PROMPT-006/008/036, despite being bound to one specific five-phase study rather than general recurring work.
findings.consequence: 4 of 13 sampled non-pilot prompts (roughly a third) have an entry-point value not supported, or contradicted, by the text cited as evidence. Because the smallest bucket (`direct-operational-entry` = 4) is the headline 'small navigable operating core' ARCH-012 leans on, a shift of even one or two prompts changes that reading materially, and the full-corpus rows (unlike the four pilot rows) carry no per-field rationale to check against.
findings.minimal_fix: Re-review the full-corpus rows' entry-point field with the same per-prompt rationale the four pilot prompts received, at least for prompts with no dependency chain or with parallel structural siblings.

findings.evidence: Read the overview's 'Chosen design' section and every child plan's 'Approach'/'Design' section (PLAN-050.01 through PLAN-050.05). findings.consequence: A reviewer applying GOV-010's content judgement cannot verify any decision in this plan family meets P2; the plan reads as assertions of what was done, not as reasoned choices among alternatives.
findings.minimal_fix: Add one sentence per material choice in the overview's 'Chosen design' section naming the rejected alternative and its cost (e.g. why not classify prompts into one composite category, why not run phases in parallel).

findings.subject: phase-bnd-07
findings.title: phase-bnd-07's scope is a system-registry edit, which ARCH-012's own next-actions table says choosing option A does not cause, and which REQ-033 R01 says the study does not do.
findings.evidence: ARCH-012 (`docs/07-architecture/ARCH-012-system-boundary-decision-report.md:105`), row for option A: "Commission a bounded follow-up to publish ownership/interface contracts and measure the identified navigation and retrieval gaps. | No package, repository split, system-registry reassignment, or prompt-status change." phase-bnd-07's scope (`docs/09-backlog/backlog.yaml:15884-15888`): "Add a required concern property to schemas/systems.schema.json... Set the concern of every entry in docs/08-governance/systems.yaml from that record, and change no other field of any entry... Add tests to test/test_governance.py for a registry entry with no concern and one with a value outside the allowed set." This is a registry edit across all 43 entries plus a schema/code change, not a document. REQ-033 R01 is more explicit still: "R01 does not reclassify the registry or edit systems.yaml; it records a proposed grouping and disposition for an owner decision" (`docs/06-requirements/REQ-033-system-boundary-study.md:44`). No requirement row in REQ-033 authorizes an actual `systems.yaml` edit; the plan's requirement-coverage table cites only the generic "R06 (the sequenced next action after each possible decision)" for phase-bnd-06 to -13, not a specific grant to mutate the registry. The plan's own "Open questions" item 3 treats even a plainly-correct registry status fix as "a registry change outside this plan" requiring separate Ideation (`PLAN-050-overview.md:155-157`), while phase-bnd-07 - registered inside this same plan - performs a registry-wide field addition and value assignment.
findings.consequence: The owner reads ARCH-012's decision gate on the understanding that choosing A causes no registry change, then finds a phase already queued under that same option to edit `systems.yaml` for every system and add an enforced schema field. If released as written, the owner's stated decision boundary is silently exceeded; if caught later, the phase has to be redone or re-scoped as a document-only proposal to match R01 and the ARCH-012 table it was supposed to implement.
findings.minimal_fix: Either amend ARCH-012's option-A row to say a registry field addition does follow from choosing A, or rescope phase-bnd-07 to produce a proposed concern mapping document (as phase-bnd-06 already does) and add a separate, later-gated phase for the owner-approved registry edit.

findings.subject: phase-bnd-08
findings.title: phase-bnd-08's scope repeats, in one session, work that the original plan split across two dedicated phases, and doubles it with an independent second classification of the whole corpus.
findings.evidence: The original plan gave rubric design and pilot its own phase (`phase-bnd-02`, scope: "Pilot the rubric against PROMPT-006, PROMPT-010, PROMPT-020, and PROMPT-040... Stop after the pilot; the complete corpus inventory is phase-bnd-05") and full-corpus application its own separate phase (`phase-bnd-05`, scope: "Apply the approved independent-field rubric to every governed prompt at its recorded baseline"), both `session_budget: 1`. phase-bnd-08's scope (`docs/09-backlog/backlog.yaml:15915-15926`) asks for all of: (1) writing a new decision rule resolving the entry-point ambiguity the 2026-09-28 validation found, (2) classifying every `kind: prompt` document (40-41 at present, per `rg -l '^kind: prompt$' docs | wc -l`) under that new rule with a cited line for each, (3) dispatching a partition-analyst to classify the same full corpus independently, (4) recording and settling every disagreement between the two classifications, and (5) publishing an index in `docs/02-prompts/README.md`. This is the scope of the original two phases combined, plus a second full independent pass and a reconciliation step, in one session.
findings.consequence: The phase is likely to blow its one-session budget or be executed shallowly (e.g., skipping the independent second classification or under-citing the reconciliation), reproducing the exact defect (F02, unjustified classification divergence) the 2026-09-28 review already found in the original single-pass corpus classification.
findings.minimal_fix: Split into two phases: one to define the entry-point rule and classify the corpus against it (mirroring phase-bnd-02/-05's split), a second to run the independent partition-analyst check, reconcile disagreements, and publish the index.

findings.subject: phase-bnd-09
findings.title: phase-bnd-09's acceptance lacks the kind of synthetic must-be-rejected case its seven sibling phases all use to satisfy GOV-010 P6.
findings.evidence: GOV-010 P6 (`docs/08-governance/GOV-010-plan-quality-standard.md:196-198`): "Acceptance names the command or observation, the expected result, and at least one input that must be rejected." phase-bnd-06, -07, -08, -10, -11, -12 and -13 each build a deliberate negative case into acceptance (a scratch copy with a row deleted that must print the missing id and exit non-zero; a registry entry with no/invalid concern that must be rejected; a cell without citation that must be changed to unknown; a diff touching forbidden paths that must be rejected). phase-bnd-09's acceptance instead reads: "A question whose expected document is not returned is recorded as a miss, not dropped or reworded" (`docs/09-backlog/backlog.yaml:15982-15984`) - an honesty-of-reporting rule about a naturally occurring outcome, not a constructed input the check must reject.
findings.consequence: A reviewer applying P6 literally to phase-bnd-09 in isolation cannot point to the same kind of fail-path evidence its siblings carry; if a miss never turns up in the twenty-question set, nothing in acceptance forces the phase to prove its own harness can detect one.
findings.minimal_fix: Add one deliberately unanswerable question to the fixed set (or use one of the retrieval gaps the portfolio review already names) so the miss case is guaranteed to exercise, not merely permitted to occur.
